title: Pope Leo to Undergo Surgery to Remove Small Growth on Lung
snippet: Pope Leo announced Sunday that he will undergo surgery this week to remove a small, early-stage lung nodule, marking the first health challenge of his papacy.
content:
VATICAN CITY — Pope Leo announced Sunday that he will undergo surgery in the coming days to remove a small growth recently discovered on his lung, marking the first major health concern since he assumed the papacy.

Addressing pilgrims gathered in St. Peter's Square for his weekly Angelus prayer, the 71-year-old pontiff sought to reassure the crowd, emphasizing that doctors caught the nodule at an early stage and that it remains "well-contained."

A Precautionary Medical Intervention

"Recently, during some medical examinations, doctors found a localized nodule in my lung," Pope Leo told the faithful. "It was detected at a very early stage and is well contained. The doctors believe it is advisable to intervene, so, following their advice, I have decided to undergo surgery to remove it."

Vatican officials did not clarify whether the nodule is suspected to be cancerous. While lung nodules are common localized lesions that are overwhelmingly benign—with the American Thoracic Society noting that fewer than 5% overall prove malignant—the risk generally increases with age.

Reassurance and Support

Elected by the College of Cardinals in May 2025, Leo is relatively young for a modern pope. Known for maintaining an active lifestyle that includes playing tennis, he has no public history of smoking or significant health ailments, presenting a distinct contrast to his late predecessor, Pope Francis, who faced mounting frailties prior to his passing at age 88.

Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni expressed her support shortly after the announcement, praising the pontiff's calm demeanor. "The serenity and composure with which he spoke about it during today’s Angelus are reassuring," Meloni said in an official statement, offering her personal support and that of the Italian government.

Impact on International Travel

The Vatican Press Office indicated that the pope's post-surgery recovery period is expected to last about a week. The brief medical pause comes as the Vatican prepares for a demanding international itinerary.

Pope Leo is currently slated to embark on an 11-day pastoral tour across Uruguay, Argentina, and Peru beginning November 6. Prior to sharing his medical update on Sunday, he asked Catholics to keep the upcoming Latin American pilgrimage in their prayers, indicating no immediate changes to his travel plans.
